answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a growing orchard of completed, verifiable work rather than a one-time credential: to reach the summit of trusted participation, an identity must tend successive tasks whose difficulty and waiting time rise with each new identity it tries to forge, and whose results are checked by different peers each time. Creating one fake is cheap, but ten parallel histories cost ten times the effort and cannot be bought in bulk, since each history is bound to its own record.
